trial.title: Comparison of the Efficacy of Ultrasound-Guided Injections of Saline, High-Concentration Dextrose, and Ligament Repair Agents for the Treatment of Medial Collateral Ligament Pathology in Degenerative Knee Osteoarthritis: A Randomized Double-Blind Trial.

endpoints.measure: Pain Reduction Using WOMAC Osteoarthritis Index
endpoints.description: The primary outcome will assess the change in pain scores using the WOMAC Osteoarthritis Index at baseline, 1 month, and 3 months after the treatment intervention
The change in knee range of motion will be measured using a goniometer at baseline, 1 month, and 3 months after intervention
The outcome will assess the change in KOOS Knee Outcome Score at baseline, 1 month, and 3 months after the treatment intervention

analysis_trace: Trial NCT06620874 is a randomized, triple-blind, parallel-group trial comparing ultrasound-guided injections of STABHA (ligament repair agent), high-concentration dextrose, and saline for medial collateral ligament pathology in knee osteoarthritis. Primary endpoint is WOMAC pain score change at 1 and 3 months; secondary endpoints include knee range of motion (goniometer) and KOOS score.

Evidence base: Retrieved PMC articles confirm dextrose prolotherapy shows WOMAC improvements of 30-50% at 24 weeks vs baseline in knee OA (PMC4357593). Rabago et al. (PMC3326267) reported 36% WOMAC improvement at 52 weeks with dextrose prolotherapy. Meta-analyses indicate dextrose prolotherapy significantly reduces pain vs saline/placebo, with effect sizes favoring active treatment.

STABHA (Soft Tissue Adapted Biocompatible Hyaluronic Acid) is a ligament-specific repair agent; no direct RCT evidence retrieved. Mechanistically, hyaluronic acid may support ligament healing but evidence in MCL-specific injection is limited. High-concentration dextrose (prolotherapy) has established efficacy for knee OA pain.
Saline placebo arm: Intra-articular saline injections in knee OA RCTs typically show 20-30% placebo response in WOMAC pain scores, with smaller effect sizes than active prolotherapy.

Population matching: Age 45-80, Kellgren-Lawrence grade 2-3, MCL grade I-II injury matches prior prolotherapy trials. Intervention differs in targeting MCL specifically vs intra-articular approaches in prior studies.

Endpoint-specific analysis: WOMAC pain (primary-0) - dextrose expected to show 25-40% improvement, STABHA uncertain (mechanism plausible but no direct evidence), saline 15-25% placebo response. Direction: dextrose > STABHA >= saline for pain reduction.
Knee ROM (secondary-0): Prolotherapy studies show modest ROM improvements (~8 degrees at 24 weeks per PMC4357593). Predict similar pattern: dextrose > saline, STABHA uncertain.
KOOS (secondary-1): Limited direct data; KOOS correlates with WOMAC. Expect parallel improvements, dextrose showing 20-35% improvement in subscales.
Confidence levels: Moderate for dextrose (consistent prior RCTs), low for STABHA (no direct evidence), moderate for saline placebo response.
Safety: Prolotherapy generally safe; minor adverse events (injection site pain, swelling) expected across arms. No serious safety signals anticipated.

Key uncertainty: STABHA is investigational with no published RCT data; efficacy inferred from hyaluronic acid mechanism and ligament repair rationale. MCL-specific injection approach differs from standard intra-articular prolotherapy.
Trial outcome prediction: Likely to demonstrate superiority of high-concentration dextrose over saline; STABHA vs saline comparison is exploratory with uncertain outcome.
